name: Zurishaddai
overview: Zurishaddai was a male member of the tribe of Simeon, noted in Scripture primarily as the father of Shelumiel. His mention is brief and focused on this familial connection without additional narrative detail. He is identified by his tribal affiliation, underscoring his place within the Israelite community.
namesAndTitles: The name Zurishaddai means 'Shaddai is [my] rock,' reflecting a declaration of God's strength and protection. This proper name, recorded in Numbers 1:6, carries a theologically rich meaning that connects the bearer to the divine attribute of God as a reliable refuge.
familyAndRelationships: Zurishaddai is explicitly identified as a descendant of Simeon and is the father of Shelumiel. Scripture does not record any other family relationships for him beyond these connections.
scriptureSignificance: Zurishaddai’s significance in the biblical narrative lies chiefly in his role as the father of Shelumiel, who is listed among the leaders of the tribe of Simeon during the wilderness census. This places Zurishaddai within the genealogical and tribal structure important for understanding Israel’s organization under God’s guidance. His name also reflects a testimony to God's power, linking his identity to the faithfulness of the Almighty.
